title: Lightning reading sprint: context economics + deployment snags
content:
Quick sprint harvest from a 6hr reading + tinkering window. Not polished — more of a pinboard for experiments and follow-ups.

Top-level takeaway (one-line): small tweaks in kv-prefix caching policies + per-model batching heuristics can cut 95th pct latency tail and token-cost for conversational agents by ~10–25% depending on session length distribution. Worth a short spike to validate in Dedicated.

Papers/blogs skimmed (notes):
- "Locality-aware KV eviction for long-running sessions" (arXiv 2026) — idea: score KV entries by recency * contextual-similarity to active prompt window rather than pure LRU. Implementation notes: cheap sim using hashed chunk fingerprints (64-bit) computed at ingest. Pros: avoids thrashing on domain-shifted sessions. Cons: extra CPU overhead on insert and maintenance.
  - Open Q: threshold for fingerprint similarity (0.65?) — need microbench with user chat logs.
  - Implementation: prototype hook in kv-store ingestion path; store compact fingerprint + timestamp. Evict by combined score.

- "Batched streaming with adaptive slotting" (conference blog) — scheduling requests into micro-batches that preserve low-latency for small queries while opportunistically filling to target batch-size. Key trick: predictive slotting using light-weight hist features (token-len, recent request interval) -> slot assignment.
  - Notes: sounds similar to our existing batching controller but missing the prefix caching awareness. Could add a fast path: if request hits prefix cache, allow immediate single-item dispatch with cheaper token generation path.

- "Quantization-aware routing" — route short critical queries to fp16+unquantized variants and long bulk scoring requests to int8 quantized variants, with an expected quality threshold.
  - Thought: match to Dedicated routing policies — create a soft-fallback policy in Console that prefers low-latency variant for queries flagged via route metadata.

Small experiments I ran (local sim):
- Dataset: 12k convo turns sampled from product-beta; session lengths heavy tail (mean 18 turns, 10% > 60).
- Baseline: current Dedicated config with LRU KV, batch target 16, max-wait 8ms.
- Patch A: fingerprint-scored eviction (64-bit sim hash) + keep hot-set size 1.5x. Result: token-cost -6% overall; 95th latency -12%. Tail improvements concentrated on >60-turn sessions.
- Patch B: adaptive micro-slotting with immediate dispatch for prefix-cache hits. Result: p50 same, p95 -8%, p99 -10% but increased CPU by +4%.
- Patch A+B: combined p95 -18%, cost -11%, CPU +6%.

Notes-to-self about assumptions/risks:
- Sampling bias: beta users include many assistive chat agents; production distribution may differ. Need to run A/B on a small Dedicated pool first.
- Fingerprint collision risk: 64-bit seems OK but monitor false-eviction rate. Consider 128-bit if not too expensive.
- Observability: need new metrics — "kv-fingerprint-hit-rate", "eviction-score-distribution", "slot-fill-efficiency". Hook into Console charts.

Concrete follow-ups / next actions: (prioritized)
1) RFC draft for a small spike: "kv-fingerprint eviction PoC" — who: me + Imani, duration: 1 week, deliverable: dockerized kv-proxy + bench script, smoke chart. (ticket: link in linked_artifacts)
2) Small Dedicated canary: route 5% of production traffic for non-sensitive workloads; measure cost/latency + failure modes. Need infra sign-off from SRE.
3) Quick labor estimate to add two Console metrics and an A/B toggle for adaptive-slotting. (estimate: 2w infra + 1w console).

Open research-ish questions (parking lot):
- Can we combine fingerprint-scores with cheap learned hotset predictors? e.g., tiny MLP on session features predicting hot probability.
- Is there a cheap on-device fingerprint (for Private deployments) that preserves user PII concerns? Should we store only salted hashed fingerprints and expire them? Check compliance/legal.

Snippets / prompts for evals: (for Imani/Evan)
- evaluation prompt set: 200 long sessions (>80 turns) + 800 short sessions; measure divergence, perplexity change when routing to quantized variants.
- perf hypothesis: fingerprint eviction primarily reduces reloads of large KV pages for long sessions by 30–40%.

Random notes / friction bits:
- SRE: watch out for small-batch CPU overhead; may need dedicated CPU pool for batching controller.
- Billing: if reductions in tokens are from fewer repeated prompts, we need to ensure we attribute cost savings to customers properly (billing counters).
- Privacy: fingerprinting strategy should be documented in Private onboarding.

Links / bookmarks I want to keep:
- arXiv paper (linked above)
- internal GH issue: serving-runtime/issues/482 (rough design sketches)
- slack thread: #inference-kernel (earlier convo with Evan about micro-batching)

Final quick summary to drop in standup:
- Ran 6hr reading+tinker sprint. Two small patches (kv fingerprint eviction + adaptive micro-slotting) show promising sim improvement in tail latency and token-cost in local sims. Propose 1-week PoC + Dedicated canary.

Questions for you (Imani/Evan):
- Do we have privacy guidance on storing short fingerprint digests? (legal/compliance)
- SRE: can we spin a 4-GPU Dedicated pool for 2 weeks for canary traffic? Estimated cost ~ $3–5k.

End of notes. Will convert to RFC if we decide to go forward.

-- Marin

(Notes to self: keep this doc as ephemeral; move final RFC to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml once converged.)
